title: Fix flaky ledger CPU test (Windows process_time granularity)
objective: Make rso.slice001.tests.test_ledger.TestCrashRowsCheat.test_context_measures_cpu deterministic on Windows without weakening what it checks: a COMPLETED run records a nonzero measured cpu_s.
problem: Reported by Argus (roles/Argus/comms/2026-10-04_DEFECT_Eupalamus_ledger_cpu_flake.md): AssertionError 0.0 not greater than 0.0 on led.inventory()[0]['cpu_s']; 4/12 isolated runs on DESKTOP-RUAPVAI, reproduced 4/10 by Palamedes on harry1. time.process_time() on Windows ticks at about 15.6 ms and the 200,000-iteration loop can finish inside one tick. It turns the acceptance command red intermittently, which T020 cannot tolerate.
non_goals: Do not weaken the assertion to >= 0.0 alone: the cheat control must still show a nonzero cpu_s is recorded
No change to ledger charging semantics or caps
evidence_required: RED: the flake reproduced (record the failing count out of N runs before the fix)
GREEN: 30 consecutive isolated runs of the test pass on Windows
the test still fails if ledger records cpu_s as 0.0 for a COMPLETED run (mutation or cheat control)

acceptance.condition: 30/30 consecutive isolated passes of test_context_measures_cpu; full suite green; the zero-cpu cheat still caught

history.note: created from Argus defect report found under T021

merged 0e7188d28; integrator on harry1: test_context_measures_cpu 20/20 isolated (was 4/10 failing); mutant cpu_s:=0.0 killed by 4 tests incl. the new fake-clock control; full suite OK (1 skipped live smoke)

notes: Argus's suggested options: spin until process_time advances (bounded), a larger fixed workload, or assert >= 0.0 plus a separate cheat control for nonzero recording. Field decision is the owner's.
